page: Amazon Web Services u-6tb1.112xlarge is an x86_64 High Memory instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, positioned for massive in-memory enterprise workloads. The system provides 448 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 224 physical cores across Intel Xeon 8176M processors operating at 2.1 GHz. It features 6144.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering approximately 13.71 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. It does not provision dedicated GPUs and provides no local storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate extreme multi-core capacity and aggregate throughput alongside moderate single-thread execution rates. Multi-core compute performance sits in the top tier, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 340,023.72 and a PassMark CPU score of 106,455.03. Aggregate memory throughput reaches 810.78 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 375.07 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, it achieved top-tier performance in Redis SET operations (297.29 million ops/sec) and static web serving throughput (100.48 GB/sec). Conversely, single-thread metrics such as the Geekbench single-core score of 1046.0 and PassMark memory score show lower efficiency relative to newer, higher-clocked processor generations.

The deployment trade-off centers on high aggregate memory capacity versus single-threaded compute density and external storage dependencies. Because the instance contains no local NVMe storage, persistent storage and high-speed I/O rely entirely on remote network-attached volumes. LLM text generation throughput is restricted by the absence of specialized accelerators, recording 8.2 tokens/sec on 7B models. From a resource perspective, the profile fits enterprise-grade in-memory operational databases (such as SAP HANA), massive memory caching grids, and large-scale data processing that require several terabytes of contiguous RAM within a single system boundary.
